prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, taking optical frequency standards to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep B007, Katori and Ye, as my preferred configuration, but my confidence is lower than in round 1 and I regard B001 as a legitimate lead. The case for B007 is one sharply defined invention: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes the light-shift problem that blocks interrogating many trapped atoms, and the realisation by Katori's group and by Ye's group took fractional uncertainty to the 10^-18 range. That changed what can be measured, which is the criterion I weigh most. The result has been reproduced and compared across several national laboratories, its interpretation is not in dispute, and the credit pair was uncontested by all eight members in the opening proposals, as the chair's summary confirms. The 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize are separate achievements on which the clocks build, and the magic-wavelength idea is separable from both.
statement.case_against: The round-1 exchange weakened some of my own arguments. I should not lean on the pending SI redefinition of the second, since that is a policy outcome and not a scientific achievement, and Olsson is right that it must not carry the case. Lindroth's point that the lattice clock may read as a refinement of an already honoured line is a fair reservation that I cannot fully answer, because much of the record 10^-18 performance also depends on ultrastable-laser and comb infrastructure outside the two names, and other Sr and Yb groups (Ludlow, Hinkley, Campbell, Takamoto) have claims the limit cannot honour. On B001, I now accept that the flat-band prediction and the observation of the correlated and superconducting phases are a robust discovery whose existence does not wait for the pairing mechanism. Six of eight members rank it first, and I do not claim that the clock's breadth of influence on physics matches that of moire quantum matter. My remaining reason to prefer B007 is that its credit is clean and its content is fixed, while B001 leaves the experimental side with one name and only a thin acknowledgment of Cao, Fatemi and the independent groups.

responses.point: Mehlig argues that the open pairing mechanism does not weaken B001, because the discovery is the flat-band prediction and the reproduced correlated and superconducting states, and waiting for a mechanism would be a stricter standard than usual.
responses.response: I concede this point and have revised my round-1 maturity argument. Prizes have gone to phenomena before their mechanism was settled, and the reproduction of the phases by several groups is the relevant evidence. What I still ask is that the citation be worded around the prediction and the observed phases, as Danielsson and Johansson say, and not imply an explanation of the superconductivity. My remaining difference with Mehlig is not maturity but what comes first when two sound candidates compete: B001 opens a field, B007 gives a new measurement capability, and I cannot show that one criterion is correct. His move to three names keeps Bistritzer, which I think is right for the joint 2011 paper.

responses.point: Pearce argues that eight years is not early for a result that has spawned a subfield, that B001 is the one case where a quantitative prediction was followed by an unambiguous experimental discovery, and that B007 is the cleaner and more mature alternative if the interpretation is judged unsettled.
responses.response: On timing I agree with Pearce that eight years is not premature, and I no longer argue that B001 should wait. B007 has the same prediction-then-realisation structure in measurement form: magic-wavelength trapping was proposed to cancel light shifts and then shown to do so at falling uncertainty. Her chair question on the deciding criterion deserves a direct answer: if the committee decides by field-opening novelty, B001 wins and I would not oppose it; if it weighs an enabling capability with fixed content and a two-name credit, B007 wins. That is a difference of values that the committee should state openly, and not hide behind support counts.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B007 first but lists as her main reservation that the lattice clock may be an improvement on the line honoured by the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and she qualifies my view of Ye's attribution as more than a continuation of comb work.
responses.response: I accept her correction on Ye: the many-body spin-exchange clock physics and the stability work are separate from the comb, and I should not have described him mainly through the Hall connection. On the 2005 and 2012 prizes I think the distinction holds. The comb is a frequency-measurement tool and ion control is a different platform, whereas many neutral atoms in a magic-wavelength lattice interrogated at once is a new route to the stability limit. I agree with her that ultrastable-laser and other-group credit is a real limitation, which is why I would word the citation on the lattice-clock invention and not on the whole optical-clock field.

responses.point: Olsson says the redefinition of the second is still pending, so the formal impact is not realised, and that my reading seems to count anticipated impact; she also moved from B030 to B001, discounting her own field.
responses.response: She is right, and I withdraw the redefinition from my argument. The scientific case stands on the demonstrated 10^-18 performance, the multi-laboratory comparisons and the tests of constants and gravitational redshift, not on a decision by the metrology community. I also respect her handling of B030: discounting a candidate in her own field is the right instinct. I would still say that the ability to measure better changes the knowledge we hold, but this is the same difference of criterion I describe in my answer to Pearce.

responses.point: Eriksson argues that the flat-band discovery does not depend on the pairing mechanism, as the 1986 cuprate discovery did not, that a prize can credit the origin of a field without naming every group, and he ranked B007 fifth partly on credit questions around other lattice-clock groups.
responses.response: His cuprate comparison is persuasive and I accept it for the maturity question. His fifth place for B007 on credit grounds is also an argument that applies to B001: the experimental credit there is a single name against a group effort with Cao as first author and several independent groups. I would not widen B001 at the expense of a theorist, as he says, but it shows that the credit problem on B001 is not smaller than the one on B007. I do not claim B007 is free of the other-group question; I claim it is more contained.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will decide by field-opening novelty or by an enabling measurement capability, which I cannot settle by evidence and which determines whether B001 or B007 leads.

Whether credit between Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's later performance and many-body milestones will be seen as co-equal, and whether other Sr and Yb groups or ultrastable-laser contributors have a claim that two names cannot accommodate.
How the committee will word B001 if it leads, in particular the experimental credit to Jarillo-Herrero alone and the precursor theory on twisted graphene.
I rely on memory rather than checked sources for the latest clock uncertainty figures and for the details of the 2005, 2012 and 2025 prizes.
statement.conflict_note: My profile documents a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during my doctoral period. In round 1 I suggested that this might connect me to Jun Ye through JILA. My profile documents no collaboration, supervision or other personal link with Ye or with Katori, and the Hall link is to the 2005 comb laureate and not to either credited name, which Lindroth also notes. In answer to the chair, I think this calls for disclosure and a record in the minutes, not recusal, but I would accept the committee's judgment and would not object to my B007 position being weighed accordingly. I also have a field proximity to atomic physics and quantum optics, including quantum-memory work in Lund, which touches B015 and B008 and could bias my views of them. I have no documented link to B001's credited names.
